Done. Here's where UK Suspense landed:

## Cleared — 7 items, £3,930.18

| Orig JE | Item | £ | Coded to |
|---|---|---|---|
| JE-00236 | Trainline rail | 84.60 | 6300 Travel |
| JE-00247 | Premier Inn (workshop) | 212.00 | 6300 Travel |
| JE-00257 | Dishoom team dinner | 96.40 | 6310 Meals & Ent. |
| JE-00259 | Atlassian | 365.00 | 6200 Software Subs |
| JE-00271 | Apple MacBook Pro | 2,349.00 | **1500 Computer Equip** |
| JE-00277 | Ryman supplies | 43.18 | 6600 Office Supplies |
| JE-00284 | Google Ads | 780.00 | 6410 Advertising |

Every receipt tied to the penny against both the ledger and the March bank statement. All entries were under the £8,000 authority limit (USD 10,000 ÷ 1.25), so no approvals needed.

**Three judgement calls worth your attention:**
- **Apple capitalized, not expensed.** £2,349 = USD 2,936 at the March rate of 1.25, clearing the USD 2,500 threshold. Depreciation starts *April* per policy, so March depreciation per DOC-0064 is unchanged — but someone needs to add asset UK-0231 to the register, which lifts the monthly charge to £1,215.25 from April.
- **Atlassian expensed, not prepaid** — receipt says monthly, so it doesn't span periods.
- **Google Ads → 6410 Advertising** rather than 6400 Marketing Programs, as it's paid search media.

## Could not clear — £3,840.00 (EXC-001)

**JE-00274 / BT-UK-0049, 17 Mar, "FASTER PAYMENT OUT REF 88213 KLM CONSULT."** I searched by vendor name, reference number, amount, and engagement terms across all entities and doc types — the only hit is the bank statement itself restating the payment. No invoice, no SOW, no approval, and KLM isn't among your recurring UK vendors.

I deliberately did **not** default it to 6520 Consulting Fees. The name is suggestive, but that's an assumption rather than evidence, and at this size a misclassification carries VAT-recovery risk too. It stays in 2900.

Two things I'd flag beyond the classification question: this was a **manual faster payment with no matching AP record**, which is worth a control look on its own; and if the service period turns out to be pre- or post-March, the right answer becomes accrual or prepaid rather than a straight expense — so I need the invoice before booking anything.

I left all checklist items open, including Bank reconciliations — these eight were the Suspense population only, and DOC-0211 has further lines I didn't reconcile under this task.
